steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: 'Artificial Things' was choreographed by Lucy Bennett for Stopgap Dance Company and premiered in 2014

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Stopgap is an integrated dance company featuring both disabled and non-disabled dancers

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The choreographic intention is to explore human connection and the idea of finding joy despite limitations

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The work celebrates difference and shows how collaboration creates something greater than individual limitations

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is the choreographic intention of 'Artificial Things'? | Q: Why is Stopgap Dance Company significant in the context of this work? | Q: How does David Toole contribute to the work?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: To explore human connection and the idea of finding joy and possibility despite limitations, celebrating how collaboration creates something greater than individual constraints. | Stopgap is an integrated company of disabled and non-disabled dancers — the work's meaning depends on this inclusive casting, as the dancers' different bodies directly embody the theme of overcoming l | David Toole is a disabled dancer whose powerful upper-body movement, floor work and expressive quality are central to the work — his performance embodies the theme of transcending physical limitations

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always mention that the company is integrated — disabled and non-disabled dancers together — this is central to the work's meaning David Toole is a key performer — be ready to describe his specific movement qualities and contribution Link the episodic structure to the work's intention: each scene explores a different aspect of human connection Include design elements: the colourful costume, varied lighting and mixed aural setting all support the themes When writing about integrated dance, focus on what the dancers can do, not what they cannot
